1.title: BankUi
1.subtitle: Mobile banking prototype
1.problem: I wanted to explore how one mobile banking interface could bring together balances in KES, USD, and BTC with local transfer flows.
1.approach: Built a Next.js and React prototype with sample balances, transfer screens, and simulated FaceID and M-Pesa flows.
1.result: The Vercel demo uses sample data. It does not connect to bank accounts or move real money.
1.metrics: Next.js 16 · React 19 · Sample KES/USD/BTC balances · Transfer demo · Simulated FaceID and M-Pesa

2.title: ArtVision
2.subtitle: Contemporary art gallery with C/WebAssembly image filters
2.problem: I wanted to make a small art gallery site that lets visitors explore images and try a few filters without a large front-end framework.
2.approach: Built a static site with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. C functions compiled to WebAssembly power grayscale, sepia, and invert filters in the image viewer.
2.result: The gallery is published on GitHub Pages. It includes responsive layouts, lazy-loaded images, and structured data.
2.metrics: C → WASM · WebP images · JSON-LD schema · Responsive (320px–4K) · Zero JS frameworks

3.title: Medimart
3.subtitle: Medical supplies shop prototype
3.problem: I built this project to try out the main parts of a small online shop for medical supplies.
3.approach: Built a React storefront and Flask API with product pages, account flows, image uploads, a scripted chat helper, and an M-Pesa sandbox payment flow.
3.result: This is a project demo, not a live medical-supplies service. The chatbot uses scripted responses, and M-Pesa is configured for sandbox testing.
3.metrics: React · Flask · Product management · Scripted chat helper · M-Pesa sandbox flow

4.title: Dotfiles
4.subtitle: My Arch Linux desktop setup
4.problem: I wanted to keep my desktop and development settings in one place so I can reuse and change them over time.
4.approach: The repository includes settings for Hyprland, Waybar, Kitty, Neovim, Starship, Tmux, Zsh, and desktop themes, plus a small sync script.
4.result: These are my personal configuration files. Review them and adapt anything you want before using them on another machine.
4.metrics: 233 tracked files · 15+ apps themed · Custom ricesync CLI · Catppuccin Mocha theme

5.title: SawaPro Landing Page
5.subtitle: A small-business landing page concept
5.problem: I wanted to build a simple web presence for a local auto repair business without adding a build step.
5.approach: Made a single-page site with HTML, Tailwind CSS from a CDN, and JavaScript. It includes a mobile menu, service cards, a gallery, and a map.
5.result: The site is a static demo. It has no booking or customer-management backend.
5.metrics: Tailwind CSS · Vanilla JS · Intersection Observer · Responsive design · Zero dependencies

6.title: DevSecOps Starter
6.subtitle: License-gated Next.js boilerplate with Paddle checkout
6.problem: I wanted a Next.js starting point with rate limiting, session checks, security headers, and deployment examples already connected.
6.approach: Built a username/password demo with PBKDF2 hashing, signed sessions, Upstash rate limiting, Supabase user storage, CSRF checks, and a one-time Paddle checkout for the starter license.
6.result: The source includes a demo flow and Paddle checkout code. Rate limiting can reduce work on downstream routes, but it is not a spend cap or DDoS protection. The source includes a license-checked download route.
6.metrics: Paddle Checkout · Rate limiting (Upstash) · Proxy role checks · PBKDF2 auth · License-gated download · CI/CD

7.title: JSON to Zustand
7.subtitle: Free dev tool — generate a Zustand store from JSON
7.problem: Setting up a Zustand store by hand means writing the state type, initial values, and setter actions. I made this tool to generate that starting code from a JSON example.
7.approach: Built a browser-based Vite and React tool that reads JSON locally, infers TypeScript types, and generates a Zustand store. The input stays in the browser.
7.result: The free tool is live at tool.fidelco.dev. It generates store code from JSON without uploading the input.
7.metrics: Vite · React · TypeScript · Zustand codegen · Zero backend · Vercel

8.title: Multi-Agent Trading
8.subtitle: Trading-strategy research prototype
8.problem: I wanted to explore whether look-ahead search and several specialized agents could work together in a trading simulation.
8.approach: Built a Python prototype with MCTS search, risk checks, transaction-cost estimates, and paper-trading support.
8.result: This is research code, not evidence of a profitable strategy. The repository includes tests and out-of-sample evaluation scripts; results depend on the data and assumptions used.
8.metrics: Multi-agent · MCTS look-ahead · Transaction-cost estimates · Python

9.title: atélier.com
9.subtitle: Furniture restoration & interior curation studio site
9.problem: I wanted to try an editorial layout for a furniture-restoration and interior-design studio.
9.approach: Built a static HTML and CSS concept with project photography, service descriptions, and a contact section.
9.result: The site is a design concept published on GitHub Pages, not a booking system or verified business listing.
9.metrics: Furniture restoration · Interior curation · Bespoke making · GitHub Pages
